- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.5) in recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast upward slightly to avoid excessive sell-off bias.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+10% from prior peak), model often overshoots and fails to mean-revert; reduce forecast peak by 5–10% and add a slight downward slope.  
- If sentiment is neutral or mildly positive (e.g., 0.0 to +0.3), model frequently underestimates upward momentum; increase forecast by 2–5% for next 3–5 days.  
- When sentiment is consistently negative over 3+ days, model tends to lag in recognizing trend reversal; add a 1–2 day lag correction to forecast, especially if true outcome shows early reversal.  
- For 30-day horizon, model often overestimates volatility in early days; cap forecast variance within 10% of recent 7-day moving average to avoid overreaction.  
- If sentiment shows strong positive momentum (e.g., >+0.4) and price is trending up, model often underestimates continuation; add 1–2% buffer to forecast for next 5–7 days.
